trg: And give me leave, And do not say 'tis superstition, that I kneel and then implore her blessing. Lady, Dear queen, that ended when I but began, Give me that hand of yours to kiss.

src: And give me leave, And do not say 'tis superstition, that I kneel and then implore her blessing. Lady, Dear queen, that ended when I but began, Give me that hand of yours to kiss.
trg: O, patience! The statue is but newly fix'd, the colour's Not dry.

src: O, patience! The statue is but newly fix'd, the colour's Not dry.
trg: My lord, your sorrow was too sore laid on, Which sixteen winters cannot blow away, So many summers dry; scarce any joy Did ever so long live; no sorrow But kill'd itself much sooner.

src: My lord, your sorrow was too sore laid on, Which sixteen winters cannot blow away, So many summers dry; scarce any joy Did ever so long live; no sorrow But kill'd itself much sooner.
trg: Dear my brother, Let him that was the cause of this have power To take off so much grief from you as he Will piece up in himself.

src: Dear my brother, Let him that was the cause of this have power To take off so much grief from you as he Will piece up in himself.
trg: Indeed, my lord, If I had thought the sight of my poor image Would thus have wrought you,--for the stone is mine-- I'ld not have show'd it.

src: Indeed, my lord, If I had thought the sight of my poor image Would thus have wrought you,--for the stone is mine-- I'ld not have show'd it.
trg: Do not draw the curtain.

src: Do not draw the curtain.
trg: No longer shall you gaze on't, lest your fancy May think anon it moves.

src: No longer shall you gaze on't, lest your fancy May think anon it moves.
trg: Let be, let be. Would I were dead, but that, methinks, already-- What was he that did make it? See, my lord, Would you not deem it breathed? and that those veins Did verily bear blood?

src: Let be, let be. Would I were dead, but that, methinks, already-- What was he that did make it? See, my lord, Would you not deem it breathed? and that those veins Did verily bear blood?
trg: Masterly done: The very life seems warm upon her lip.

src: Masterly done: The very life seems warm upon her lip.
trg: The fixture of her eye has motion in't, As we are mock'd with art.

src: The fixture of her eye has motion in't, As we are mock'd with art.
trg: I'll draw the curtain: My lord's almost so far transported that He'll think anon it lives.

src: I'll draw the curtain: My lord's almost so far transported that He'll think anon it lives.
trg: O sweet Paulina, Make me to think so twenty years together! No settled senses of the world can match The pleasure of that madness. Let 't alone.

src: O sweet Paulina, Make me to think so twenty years together! No settled senses of the world can match The pleasure of that madness. Let 't alone.
trg: I am sorry, sir, I have thus far stirr'd you: but I could afflict you farther.

src: I am sorry, sir, I have thus far stirr'd you: but I could afflict you farther.
trg: Do, Paulina; For this affliction has a taste as sweet As any cordial comfort. Still, methinks, There is an air comes from her: what fine chisel Could ever yet cut breath? Let no man mock me, For I will kiss her.

src: Do, Paulina; For this affliction has a taste as sweet As any cordial comfort. Still, methinks, There is an air comes from her: what fine chisel Could ever yet cut breath? Let no man mock me, For I will kiss her.
trg: Good my lord, forbear: The ruddiness upon her lip is wet; You'll mar it if you kiss it, stain your own With oily painting. Shall I draw the curtain?

src: Good my lord, forbear: The ruddiness upon her lip is wet; You'll mar it if you kiss it, stain your own With oily painting. Shall I draw the curtain?
trg: No, not these twenty years.

src: No, not these twenty years.
trg: So long could I Stand by, a looker on.

src: So long could I Stand by, a looker on.
trg: Either forbear, Quit presently the chapel, or resolve you For more amazement. If you can behold it, I'll make the statue move indeed, descend And take you by the hand; but then you'll think-- Which I protest against--I am assisted By wicked powers.

src: Either forbear, Quit presently the chapel, or resolve you For more amazement. If you can behold it, I'll make the statue move indeed, descend And take you by the hand; but then you'll think-- Which I protest against--I am assisted By wicked powers.
trg: What you can make her do, I am content to look on: what to speak, I am content to hear; for 'tis as easy To make her speak as move.

src: What you can make her do, I am content to look on: what to speak, I am content to hear; for 'tis as easy To make her speak as move.
trg: It is required You do awake your faith. Then all stand still; On: those that think it is unlawful business I am about, let them depart.

src: It is required You do awake your faith. Then all stand still; On: those that think it is unlawful business I am about, let them depart.
trg: Proceed: No foot shall stir.

src: Proceed: No foot shall stir.
trg: Music, awake her; strike! 'Tis time; descend; be stone no more; approach; Strike all that look upon with marvel. Come, I'll fill your grave up: stir, nay, come away, Bequeath to death your numbness, for from him Dear life redeems you. You perceive she stirs: Start not; her actions shall be holy as You hear my spell is lawful: do not shun her Until you see her die again; for then You kill her double. Nay, present your hand: When she was young you woo'd her; now in age Is she become the suitor?

src: Music, awake her; strike! 'Tis time; descend; be stone no more; approach; Strike all that look upon with marvel. trg: O, she's warm! If this be magic, let it be an art Lawful as eating.

src: O, she's warm! If this be magic, let it be an art Lawful as eating.
trg: She embraces him.

src: She embraces him.
trg: She hangs about his neck: If she pertain to life let her speak too.

src: She hangs about his neck: If she pertain to life let her speak too.
trg: Ay, and make't manifest where she has lived, Or how stolen from the dead.

src: Ay, and make't manifest where she has lived, Or how stolen from the dead.
trg: That she is living, Were it but told you, should be hooted at Like an old tale: but it appears she lives, Though yet she speak not. Mark a little while. Please you to interpose, fair madam: kneel And pray your mother's blessing. Turn, good lady; Our Perdita is found.

src: That she is living, Were it but told you, should be hooted at Like an old tale: but it appears she lives, Though yet she speak not. Mark a little while. Please you to interpose, fair madam: kneel And pray your mother's blessing. Turn, good lady; Our Perdita is found.
trg: You gods, look down And from your sacred vials pour your graces Upon my daughter's head! Tell me, mine own. Where hast thou been preserved? where lived? how found Thy father's court? for thou shalt hear that I, Knowing by Paulina that the oracle Gave hope thou wast in being, have preserved Myself to see the issue.

src: You gods, look down And from your sacred vials pour your graces Upon my daughter's head! Tell me, mine own. Where hast thou been preserved? where lived? how found Thy father's court? for thou shalt hear that I, Knowing by Paulina that the oracle Gave hope thou wast in being, have preserved Myself to see the issue.
trg: There's time enough for that; Lest they desire upon this push to trouble Your joys with like relation. Go together, You precious winners all; your exultation Partake to every one. I, an old turtle, Will wing me to some wither'd bough and there My mate, that's never to be found again, Lament till I am lost.

trg: O, peace, Paulina! Thou shouldst a husband take by my consent, As I by thine a wife: this is a match, And made between's by vows. Thou hast found mine; But how, is to be question'd; for I saw her, As I thought, dead, and have in vain said many A prayer upon her grave. I'll not seek far-- For him, I partly know his mind--to find thee An honourable husband. Come, Camillo, And take her by the hand, whose worth and honesty Is richly noted and here justified By us, a pair of kings. Let's from this place. What! look upon my brother: both your pardons, That e'er I put between your holy looks My ill suspicion. This is your son-in-law, And son unto the king, who, heavens directing, Is troth-plight to your daughter. Good Paulina, Lead us from hence, where we may leisurely Each one demand an answer to his part Perform'd in this wide gap of time since first We were dissever'd: hastily lead away.

trg: Escalus.

src: Escalus.
trg: My lord.

src: My lord.
trg: Of government the properties to unfold, Would seem in me to affect speech and discourse; Since I am put to know that your own science Exceeds, in that, the lists of all advice My strength can give you: then no more remains, But that to your sufficiency, as your Worth is able, And let them work. The nature of our people, Our city's institutions, and the terms For common justice, you're as pregnant in As art and practise hath enriched any That we remember. There is our commission, From which we would not have you warp. Call hither, I say, bid come before us Angelo. What figure of us think you he will bear? For you must know, we have with special soul Elected him our absence to supply, Lent him our terror, dress'd him with our love, And given his deputation all the organs Of our own power: what think you of it?

trg: Look where he comes.

src: Look where he comes.
trg: Always obedient to your grace's will, I come to know your pleasure.

src: Always obedient to your grace's will, I come to know your pleasure.
trg: Angelo, There is a kind of character in thy life, That to the observer doth thy history Fully unfold. Thyself and thy belongings Are not thine own so proper as to waste Thyself upon thy virtues, they on thee. Heaven doth with us as we with torches do, Not light them for themselves; for if our virtues Did not go forth of us, 'twere all alike As if we had them not. Spirits are not finely touch'd But to fine issues, nor Nature never lends The smallest scruple of her excellence But, like a thrifty goddess, she determines Herself the glory of a creditor, Both thanks and use. But I do bend my speech To one that can my part in him advertise; Hold therefore, Angelo:-- In our remove be thou at full ourself; Mortality and mercy in Vienna Live in thy tongue and heart: old Escalus, Though first in question, is thy secondary. Take thy commission.

trg: Now, good my lord, Let there be some more test made of my metal, Before so noble and so great a figure Be stamp'd upon it.

src: Now, good my lord, Let there be some more test made of my metal, Before so noble and so great a figure Be stamp'd upon it.
trg: No more evasion: We have with a leaven'd and prepared choice Proceeded to you; therefore take your honours. Our haste from hence is of so quick condition That it prefers itself and leaves unquestion'd Matters of needful value. We shall write to you, As time and our concernings shall importune, How it goes with us, and do look to know What doth befall you here. So, fare you well; To the hopeful execution do I leave you Of your commissions.

trg: Yet give leave, my lord, That we may bring you something on the way.

src: Yet give leave, my lord, That we may bring you something on the way.
trg: My haste may not admit it; Nor need you, on mine honour, have to do With any scruple; your scope is as mine own So to enforce or qualify the laws As to your soul seems good. Give me your hand: I'll privily away. I love the people, But do not like to stage me to their eyes: Through it do well, I do not relish well Their loud applause and Aves vehement; Nor do I think the man of safe discretion That does affect it. Once more, fare you well.

src: I thank you. Fare you well.
trg: I shall desire you, sir, to give me leave To have free speech with you; and it concerns me To look into the bottom of my place: A power I have, but of what strength and nature I am not yet instructed.

trg: I'll wait upon your honour.

src: I'll wait upon your honour.
trg: If the duke with the other dukes come not to composition with the King of Hungary, why then all the dukes fall upon the king.

trg: Heaven grant us its peace, but not the King of Hungary's!

src: Heaven grant us its peace, but not the King of Hungary's!
trg: Amen.

src: Amen.
trg: Thou concludest like the sanctimonious pirate, that went to sea with the Ten Commandments, but scraped one out of the table.

trg: 'Thou shalt not steal'?

src: 'Thou shalt not steal'?

src: Ay, that he razed.
trg: Why, 'twas a commandment to command the captain and all the rest from their functions: they put forth to steal. There's not a soldier of us all, that, in the thanksgiving before meat, do relish the petition well that prays for peace.

trg: I believe thee; for I think thou never wast where grace was said.

trg: Well, there went but a pair of shears between us.

trg: I grant; as there may between the lists and the velvet. Thou art the list.

src: I grant; as there may between the lists and the velvet. Thou art the list.
trg: And thou the velvet: thou art good velvet; thou'rt a three-piled piece, I warrant thee: I had as lief be a list of an English kersey as be piled, as thou art piled, for a French velvet. Do I speak feelingly now?

trg: I think thou dost; and, indeed, with most painful feeling of thy speech: I will, out of thine own confession, learn to begin thy health; but, whilst I live, forget to drink after thee.

trg: We have strict statutes and most biting laws. The needful bits and curbs to headstrong weeds, Which for this nineteen years we have let slip; Even like an o'ergrown lion in a cave, That goes not out to prey. Now, as fond fathers, Having bound up the threatening twigs of birch, Only to stick it in their children's sight For terror, not to use, in time the rod Becomes more mock'd than fear'd; so our decrees, Dead to infliction, to themselves are dead; And liberty plucks justice by the nose; The baby beats the nurse, and quite athwart Goes all decorum.

trg: I do fear, too dreadful: Sith 'twas my fault to give the people scope, 'Twould be my tyranny to strike and gall them For what I bid them do: for we bid this be done, When evil deeds have their permissive pass And not the punishment. Therefore indeed, my father, I have on Angelo imposed the office; Who may, in the ambush of my name, strike home, And yet my nature never in the fight To do in slander. And to behold his sway, I will, as 'twere a brother of your order, Visit both prince and people: therefore, I prithee, Supply me with the habit and instruct me How I may formally in person bear me Like a true friar. More reasons for this action At our more leisure shall I render you; Only, this one: Lord Angelo is precise; Stands at a guard with envy; scarce confesses That his blood flows, or that his appetite Is more to bread than stone: hence shall we see, If power change purpose, what our seemers be.

trg: This is the point. The duke is very strangely gone from hence; Bore many gentlemen, myself being one, In hand and hope of action: but we do learn By those that know the very nerves of state, His givings-out were of an infinite distance From his true-meant design. Upon his place, And with full line of his authority, Governs Lord Angelo; a man whose blood Is very snow-broth; one who never feels The wanton stings and motions of the sense, But doth rebate and blunt his natural edge With profits of the mind, study and fast. He--to give fear to use and liberty, Which have for long run by the hideous law, As mice by lions--hath pick'd out an act, Under whose heavy sense your brother's life Falls into forfeit: he arrests him on it; And follows close the rigour of the statute, To make him an example. All hope is gone, Unless you have the grace by your fair prayer To soften Angelo: and that's my pith of business 'Twixt you and your poor brother.

trg: 'Tis one thing to be tempted, Escalus, Another thing to fall. I not deny, The jury, passing on the prisoner's life, May in the sworn twelve have a thief or two Guiltier than him they try. What's open made to justice, That justice seizes: what know the laws That thieves do pass on thieves? 'Tis very pregnant, The jewel that we find, we stoop and take't Because we see it; but what we do not see We tread upon, and never think of it. You may not so extenuate his offence For I have had such faults; but rather tell me, When I, that censure him, do so offend, Let mine own judgment pattern out my death, And nothing come in partial. Sir, he must die.

src: He, sir! a tapster, sir; parcel-bawd; one that serves a bad woman; whose house, sir, was, as they say, plucked down in the suburbs; and now she professes a hot-house, which, I think, is a very ill house too.
trg: How know you that?

src: How know you that?
trg: My wife, sir, whom I detest before heaven and your honour,--

src: My wife, sir, whom I detest before heaven and your honour,--
trg: How? thy wife?

src: How? thy wife?
trg: Ay, sir; whom, I thank heaven, is an honest woman,--

src: Ay, sir; whom, I thank heaven, is an honest woman,--
trg: Dost thou detest her therefore?

src: Dost thou detest her therefore?
trg: I say, sir, I will detest myself also, as well as she, that this house, if it be not a bawd's house, it is pity of her life, for it is a naughty house.

src: I say, sir, I will detest myself also, as well as she, that this house, if it be not a bawd's house, it is pity of her life, for it is a naughty house.
trg: How dost thou know that, constable?

src: How dost thou know that, constable?
trg: Marry, sir, by my wife; who, if she had been a woman cardinally given, might have been accused in fornication, adultery, and all uncleanliness there.

src: Marry, sir, by my wife; who, if she had been a woman cardinally given, might have been accused in fornication, adultery, and all uncleanliness there.
trg: By the woman's means?

src: By the woman's means?
trg: Ay, sir, by Mistress Overdone's means: but as she spit in his face, so she defied him.

src: Ay, sir, by Mistress Overdone's means: but as she spit in his face, so she defied him.
trg: Sir, if it please your honour, this is not so.

src: Sir, if it please your honour, this is not so.
trg: Prove it before these varlets here, thou honourable man; prove it.

src: Prove it before these varlets here, thou honourable man; prove it.
trg: Do you hear how he misplaces?

src: Do you hear how he misplaces?
trg: Sir, she came in great with child; and longing, saving your honour's reverence, for stewed prunes; sir, we had but two in the house, which at that very distant time stood, as it were, in a fruit-dish, a dish of some three-pence; your honours have seen such dishes; they are not China dishes, but very good dishes,--

src: Sir, she came in great with child; and longing, saving your honour's reverence, for stewed prunes; sir, we had but two in the house, which at that very distant time stood, as it were, in a fruit-dish, a dish of some three-pence; your honours have seen such dishes; they are not China dishes, but very good dishes,--
trg: Go to, go to: no matter for the dish, sir.

src: Go to, go to: no matter for the dish, sir.
trg: No, indeed, sir, not of a pin; you are therein in the right: but to the point. As I say, this Mistress Elbow, being, as I say, with child, and being great-bellied, and longing, as I said, for prunes; and having but two in the dish, as I said, Master Froth here, this very man, having eaten the rest, as I said, and, as I say, paying for them very honestly; for, as you know, Master Froth, I could not give you three-pence again.

src: No, indeed, sir, not of a pin; you are therein in the right: but to the point. As I say, this Mistress Elbow, being, as I say, with child, and being great-bellied, and longing, as I said, for prunes; and having but two in the dish, as I said, Master Froth here, this very man, having eaten the rest, as I said, and, as I say, paying for them very honestly; for, as you know, Master Froth, I could not give you three-pence again.
trg: No, indeed.

src: No, indeed.
trg: Very well: you being then, if you be remembered, cracking the stones of the foresaid prunes,--

src: Very well: you being then, if you be remembered, cracking the stones of the foresaid prunes,--
trg: Ay, so I did indeed.

src: Ay, so I did indeed.
trg: Why, very well; I telling you then, if you be remembered, that such a one and such a one were past cure of the thing you wot of, unless they kept very good diet, as I told you,--

src: Why, very well; I telling you then, if you be remembered, that such a one and such a one were past cure of the thing you wot of, unless they kept very good diet, as I told you,--
trg: All this is true.

src: All this is true.
trg: Why, very well, then,--

src: Why, very well, then,--
trg: Come, you are a tedious fool: to the purpose. What was done to Elbow's wife, that he hath cause to complain of? Come me to what was done to her.

src: Come, you are a tedious fool: to the purpose. What was done to Elbow's wife, that he hath cause to complain of? Come me to what was done to her.
trg: Sir, your honour cannot come to that yet.

src: Sir, your honour cannot come to that yet.
trg: No, sir, nor I mean it not.

src: No, sir, nor I mean it not.
trg: Sir, but you shall come to it, by your honour's leave. And, I beseech you, look into Master Froth here, sir; a man of four-score pound a year; whose father died at Hallowmas: was't not at Hallowmas, Master Froth?

src: Sir, but you shall come to it, by your honour's leave. And, I beseech you, look into Master Froth here, sir; a man of four-score pound a year; whose father died at Hallowmas: was't not at Hallowmas, Master Froth?
trg: All-hallond eve.

src: All-hallond eve.
trg: Why, very well; I hope here be truths. He, sir, sitting, as I say, in a lower chair, sir; 'twas in the Bunch of Grapes, where indeed you have a delight to sit, have you not?

src: Why, very well; I hope here be truths. He, sir, sitting, as I say, in a lower chair, sir; 'twas in the Bunch of Grapes, where indeed you have a delight to sit, have you not?
trg: I have so; because it is an open room and good for winter.

src: I have so; because it is an open room and good for winter.
trg: Why, very well, then; I hope here be truths.

src: Why, very well, then; I hope here be truths.
trg: This will last out a night in Russia, When nights are longest there: I'll take my leave. And leave you to the hearing of the cause; Hoping you'll find good cause to whip them all.

src: This will last out a night in Russia, When nights are longest there: I'll take my leave. And leave you to the hearing of the cause; Hoping you'll find good cause to whip them all.
trg: I think no less. Good morrow to your lordship. Now, sir, come on: what was done to Elbow's wife, once more?

src: I think no less. Good morrow to your lordship. Now, sir, come on: what was done to Elbow's wife, once more?
trg: Once, sir? there was nothing done to her once.

src: Once, sir? there was nothing done to her once.
trg: I beseech you, sir, ask him what this man did to my wife.

src: I beseech you, sir, ask him what this man did to my wife.
trg: I beseech your honour, ask me.

src: I beseech your honour, ask me.
trg: Well, sir; what did this gentleman to her?

src: Well, sir; what did this gentleman to her?
trg: I beseech you, sir, look in this gentleman's face. Good Master Froth, look upon his honour; 'tis for a good purpose. Doth your honour mark his face?

src: I beseech you, sir, look in this gentleman's face. Good Master Froth, look upon his honour; 'tis for a good purpose. Doth your honour mark his face?
trg: Ay, sir, very well.

src: Ay, sir, very well.
trg: Nay; I beseech you, mark it well.

src: Nay; I beseech you, mark it well.
trg: Well, I do so.

src: Well, I do so.
trg: Doth your honour see any harm in his face?

src: Doth your honour see any harm in his face?
trg: Why, no.

src: Why, no.
trg: I'll be supposed upon a book, his face is the worst thing about him. Good, then; if his face be the worst thing about him, how could Master Froth do the constable's wife any harm? I would know that of your honour.

src: I'll be supposed upon a book, his face is the worst thing about him. Good, then; if his face be the worst thing about him, how could Master Froth do the constable's wife any harm? I would know that of your honour.
trg: He's in the right. Constable, what say you to it?

src: He's in the right. Constable, what say you to it?
trg: First, an it like you, the house is a respected house; next, this is a respected fellow; and his mistress is a respected woman.

src: First, an it like you, the house is a respected house; next, this is a respected fellow; and his mistress is a respected woman.
trg: By this hand, sir, his wife is a more respected person than any of us all.

src: By this hand, sir, his wife is a more respected person than any of us all.
trg: Varlet, thou liest; thou liest, wicked varlet! the time has yet to come that she was ever respected with man, woman, or child.

src: Varlet, thou liest; thou liest, wicked varlet! the time has yet to come that she was ever respected with man, woman, or child.
trg: Sir, she was respected with him before he married with her.

src: Sir, she was respected with him before he married with her.
trg: Which is the wiser here? Justice or Iniquity? Is this true?

src: Which is the wiser here? Justice or Iniquity? Is this true?
trg: O thou caitiff! O thou varlet! O thou wicked Hannibal! I respected with her before I was married to her! If ever I was respected with her, or she with me, let not your worship think me the poor duke's officer. Prove this, thou wicked Hannibal, or I'll have mine action of battery on thee.

src: O thou caitiff! O thou varlet! O thou wicked Hannibal! I respected with her before I was married to her! If ever I was respected with her, or she with me, let not your worship think me the poor duke's officer. Prove this, thou wicked Hannibal, or I'll have mine action of battery on thee.
trg: If he took you a box o' the ear, you might have your action of slander too.

src: If he took you a box o' the ear, you might have your action of slander too.
trg: Marry, I thank your good worship for it. What is't your worship's pleasure I shall do with this wicked caitiff?

src: Marry, I thank your good worship for it. What is't your worship's pleasure I shall do with this wicked caitiff?
trg: Truly, officer, because he hath some offences in him that thou wouldst discover if thou couldst, let him continue in his courses till thou knowest what they are.

src: Truly, officer, because he hath some offences in him that thou wouldst discover if thou couldst, let him continue in his courses till thou knowest what they are.
trg: Marry, I thank your worship for it. Thou seest, thou wicked varlet, now, what's come upon thee: thou art to continue now, thou varlet; thou art to continue.

src: Marry, I thank your worship for it. Thou seest, thou wicked varlet, now, what's come upon thee: thou art to continue now, thou varlet; thou art to continue.
trg: Where were you born, friend?

src: Where were you born, friend?
trg: Here in Vienna, sir.

src: Here in Vienna, sir.
trg: Are you of fourscore pounds a year?

src: Are you of fourscore pounds a year?
trg: Yes, an't please you, sir.

src: Yes, an't please you, sir.
trg: So. What trade are you of, sir?

src: So. What trade are you of, sir?
trg: Tapster; a poor widow's tapster.

src: Tapster; a poor widow's tapster.
trg: Your mistress' name?

src: Your mistress' name?
trg: Mistress Overdone.

src: Mistress Overdone.
trg: Hath she had any more than one husband?

src: Hath she had any more than one husband?
trg: Nine, sir; Overdone by the last.

src: Nine, sir; Overdone by the last.
trg: Nine! Come hither to me, Master Froth. Master Froth, I would not have you acquainted with tapsters: they will draw you, Master Froth, and you will hang them. Get you gone, and let me hear no more of you.

src: Nine! Come hither to me, Master Froth. Master Froth, I would not have you acquainted with tapsters: they will draw you, Master Froth, and you will hang them. Get you gone, and let me hear no more of you.
trg: I thank your worship. For mine own part, I never come into any room in a tap-house, but I am drawn in.

src: I thank your worship. For mine own part, I never come into any room in a tap-house, but I am drawn in.
trg: Well, no more of it, Master Froth: farewell. Come you hither to me, Master tapster. What's your name, Master tapster?

src: Well, no more of it, Master Froth: farewell. Come you hither to me, Master tapster. What's your name, Master tapster?
trg: Pompey.

src: Pompey.
trg: What else?

src: What else?
trg: Bum, sir.

src: Bum, sir.
trg: Troth, and your bum is the greatest thing about you; so that in the beastliest sense you are Pompey the Great. Pompey, you are partly a bawd, Pompey, howsoever you colour it in being a tapster, are you not? come, tell me true: it shall be the better for you.

src: Troth, and your bum is the greatest thing about you; so that in the beastliest sense you are Pompey the Great. Pompey, you are partly a bawd, Pompey, howsoever you colour it in being a tapster, are you not? come, tell me true: it shall be the better for you.
trg: Truly, sir, I am a poor fellow that would live.

src: Truly, sir, I am a poor fellow that would live.
trg: How would you live, Pompey? by being a bawd? What do you think of the trade, Pompey? is it a lawful trade?

src: How would you live, Pompey? by being a bawd? What do you think of the trade, Pompey? is it a lawful trade?
trg: If the law would allow it, sir.

src: If the law would allow it, sir.
trg: But the law will not allow it, Pompey; nor it shall not be allowed in Vienna.

src: But the law will not allow it, Pompey; nor it shall not be allowed in Vienna.
trg: Does your worship mean to geld and splay all the youth of the city?

src: Does your worship mean to geld and splay all the youth of the city?
trg: No, Pompey.

src: No, Pompey.
trg: Truly, sir, in my poor opinion, they will to't then. If your worship will take order for the drabs and the knaves, you need not to fear the bawds.

src: Truly, sir, in my poor opinion, they will to't then. If your worship will take order for the drabs and the knaves, you need not to fear the bawds.
trg: There are pretty orders beginning, I can tell you: it is but heading and hanging.

src: There are pretty orders beginning, I can tell you: it is but heading and hanging.
trg: If you head and hang all that offend that way but for ten year together, you'll be glad to give out a commission for more heads: if this law hold in Vienna ten year, I'll rent the fairest house in it after three-pence a bay: if you live to see this come to pass, say Pompey told you so.

src: If you head and hang all that offend that way but for ten year together, you'll be glad to give out a commission for more heads: if this law hold in Vienna ten year, I'll rent the fairest house in it after three-pence a bay: if you live to see this come to pass, say Pompey told you so.
trg: Thank you, good Pompey; and, in requital of your prophecy, hark you: I advise you, let me not find you before me again upon any complaint whatsoever; no, not for dwelling where you do: if I do, Pompey, I shall beat you to your tent, and prove a shrewd Caesar to you; in plain dealing, Pompey, I shall have you whipt: so, for this time, Pompey, fare you well.

src: Thank you, good Pompey; and, in requital of your prophecy, hark you: I advise you, let me not find you before me again upon any complaint whatsoever; no, not for dwelling where you do: if I do, Pompey, I shall beat you to your tent, and prove a shrewd Caesar to you; in plain dealing, Pompey, I shall have you whipt: so, for this time, Pompey, fare you well.
trg: I thank your worship for your good counsel: but I shall follow it as the flesh and fortune shall better determine. Whip me? No, no; let carman whip his jade: The valiant heart is not whipt out of his trade.

src: I thank your worship for your good counsel: but I shall follow it as the flesh and fortune shall better determine. Whip me? No, no; let carman whip his jade: The valiant heart is not whipt out of his trade.
trg: Come hither to me, Master Elbow; come hither, Master constable. How long have you been in this place of constable?

src: Come hither to me, Master Elbow; come hither, Master constable. How long have you been in this place of constable?
trg: Seven year and a half, sir.

src: Seven year and a half, sir.
trg: I thought, by your readiness in the office, you had continued in it some time. You say, seven years together?

src: I thought, by your readiness in the office, you had continued in it some time. You say, seven years together?
trg: And a half, sir.

src: And a half, sir.
trg: Alas, it hath been great pains to you. They do you wrong to put you so oft upon 't: are there not men in your ward sufficient to serve it?

src: Alas, it hath been great pains to you. They do you wrong to put you so oft upon 't: are there not men in your ward sufficient to serve it?
trg: Faith, sir, few of any wit in such matters: as they are chosen, they are glad to choose me for them; I do it for some piece of money, and go through with all.

src: Faith, sir, few of any wit in such matters: as they are chosen, they are glad to choose me for them; I do it for some piece of money, and go through with all.
trg: Look you bring me in the names of some six or seven, the most sufficient of your parish.

src: Look you bring me in the names of some six or seven, the most sufficient of your parish.
trg: To your worship's house, sir?

src: To your worship's house, sir?
trg: To my house. Fare you well. What's o'clock, think you?

src: To my house. Fare you well. What's o'clock, think you?
trg: Eleven, sir.

src: Eleven, sir.
trg: I pray you home to dinner with me.

src: I pray you home to dinner with me.
trg: I humbly thank you.

src: I humbly thank you.
trg: It grieves me for the death of Claudio; But there's no remedy.

src: It grieves me for the death of Claudio; But there's no remedy.
trg: Lord Angelo is severe.

src: Lord Angelo is severe.
trg: It is but needful: Mercy is not itself, that oft looks so; Pardon is still the nurse of second woe: But yet,--poor Claudio! There is no remedy. Come, sir.

src: It is but needful: Mercy is not itself, that oft looks so; Pardon is still the nurse of second woe: But yet,--poor Claudio! There is no remedy. Come, sir.
trg: He's hearing of a cause; he will come straight I'll tell him of you.

src: He's hearing of a cause; he will come straight I'll tell him of you.
trg: Pray you, do. I'll know His pleasure; may be he will relent. Alas, He hath but as offended in a dream! All sects, all ages smack of this vice; and he To die for't!

src: Pray you, do. I'll know His pleasure; may be he will relent. Alas, He hath but as offended in a dream! All sects, all ages smack of this vice; and he To die for't!
trg: Now, what's the matter. Provost?

src: Now, what's the matter. Provost?
trg: Is it your will Claudio shall die tomorrow?

src: Is it your will Claudio shall die tomorrow?
trg: Did not I tell thee yea? hadst thou not order? Why dost thou ask again?

src: Did not I tell thee yea? hadst thou not order? Why dost thou ask again?
trg: Lest I might be too rash: Under your good correction, I have seen, When, after execution, judgment hath Repented o'er his doom.

src: Lest I might be too rash: Under your good correction, I have seen, When, after execution, judgment hath Repented o'er his doom.
trg: Go to; let that be mine: Do you your office, or give up your place, And you shall well be spared.

src: Go to; let that be mine: Do you your office, or give up your place, And you shall well be spared.
trg: I crave your honour's pardon. What shall be done, sir, with the groaning Juliet? She's very near her hour.

src: I crave your honour's pardon. What shall be done, sir, with the groaning Juliet? She's very near her hour.
trg: Dispose of her To some more fitter place, and that with speed.

src: Dispose of her To some more fitter place, and that with speed.
trg: Here is the sister of the man condemn'd Desires access to you.

src: Here is the sister of the man condemn'd Desires access to you.
trg: Hath he a sister?

src: Hath he a sister?
trg: Ay, my good lord; a very virtuous maid, And to be shortly of a sisterhood, If not already.

src: Ay, my good lord; a very virtuous maid, And to be shortly of a sisterhood, If not already.
trg: Well, let her be admitted. See you the fornicatress be removed: Let have needful, but not lavish, means; There shall be order for't.

src: Well, let her be admitted. See you the fornicatress be removed: Let have needful, but not lavish, means; There shall be order for't.
trg: God save your honour!

src: God save your honour!
trg: Stay a little while. You're welcome: what's your will?

src: Stay a little while. You're welcome: what's your will?
trg: I am a woeful suitor to your honour, Please but your honour hear me.

src: I am a woeful suitor to your honour, Please but your honour hear me.
trg: Well; what's your suit?

src: Well; what's your suit?
trg: There is a vice that most I do abhor, And most desire should meet the blow of justice; For which I would not plead, but that I must; For which I must not plead, but that I am At war 'twixt will and will not.

src: There is a vice that most I do abhor, And most desire should meet the blow of justice; For which I would not plead, but that I must; For which I must not plead, but that I am At war 'twixt will and will not.
trg: Well; the matter?

src: Well; the matter?
trg: I have a brother is condemn'd to die: I do beseech you, let it be his fault, And not my brother.

src: I have a brother is condemn'd to die: I do beseech you, let it be his fault, And not my brother.

trg: Condemn the fault and not the actor of it? Why, every fault's condemn'd ere it be done: Mine were the very cipher of a function, To fine the faults whose fine stands in record, And let go by the actor.

src: Condemn the fault and not the actor of it? Why, every fault's condemn'd ere it be done: Mine were the very cipher of a function, To fine the faults whose fine stands in record, And let go by the actor.
trg: O just but severe law! I had a brother, then. Heaven keep your honour!

src: O just but severe law! I had a brother, then. Heaven keep your honour!

trg: Must he needs die?

src: Must he needs die?
trg: Maiden, no remedy.

src: Maiden, no remedy.
trg: Yes; I do think that you might pardon him, And neither heaven nor man grieve at the mercy.

src: Yes; I do think that you might pardon him, And neither heaven nor man grieve at the mercy.
trg: I will not do't.

src: I will not do't.
trg: But can you, if you would?

src: But can you, if you would?
trg: Look, what I will not, that I cannot do.

src: Look, what I will not, that I cannot do.
trg: But might you do't, and do the world no wrong, If so your heart were touch'd with that remorse As mine is to him?

src: But might you do't, and do the world no wrong, If so your heart were touch'd with that remorse As mine is to him?
trg: He's sentenced; 'tis too late.

src: He's sentenced; 'tis too late.

trg: Too late? why, no; I, that do speak a word. May call it back again. Well, believe this, No ceremony that to great ones 'longs, Not the king's crown, nor the deputed sword, The marshal's truncheon, nor the judge's robe, Become them with one half so good a grace As mercy does. If he had been as you and you as he, You would have slipt like him; but he, like you, Would not have been so stern.

src: Too late? why, no; I, that do speak a word. May call it back again. Well, believe this, No ceremony that to great ones 'longs, Not the king's crown, nor the deputed sword, The marshal's truncheon, nor the judge's robe, Become them with one half so good a grace As mercy does. If he had been as you and you as he, You would have slipt like him; but he, like you, Would not have been so stern.
trg: Pray you, be gone.

src: Pray you, be gone.
trg: I would to heaven I had your potency, And you were Isabel! should it then be thus? No; I would tell what 'twere to be a judge, And what a prisoner.

src: I would to heaven I had your potency, And you were Isabel! should it then be thus? No; I would tell what 'twere to be a judge, And what a prisoner.

trg: Your brother is a forfeit of the law, And you but waste your words.

src: Your brother is a forfeit of the law, And you but waste your words.
trg: Alas, alas! Why, all the souls that were were forfeit once; And He that might the vantage best have took Found out the remedy. How would you be, If He, which is the top of judgment, should But judge you as you are? O, think on that; And mercy then will breathe within your lips, Like man new made.

src: Alas, alas! Why, all the souls that were were forfeit once; And He that might the vantage best have took Found out the remedy. How would you be, If He, which is the top of judgment, should But judge you as you are? O, think on that; And mercy then will breathe within your lips, Like man new made.
trg: Be you content, fair maid; It is the law, not I condemn your brother: Were he my kinsman, brother, or my son, It should be thus with him: he must die tomorrow.

src: Be you content, fair maid; It is the law, not I condemn your brother: Were he my kinsman, brother, or my son, It should be thus with him: he must die tomorrow.
trg: To-morrow! O, that's sudden! Spare him, spare him! He's not prepared for death. Even for our kitchens We kill the fowl of season: shall we serve heaven With less respect than we do minister To our gross selves? Good, good my lord, bethink you; Who is it that hath died for this offence? There's many have committed it.

src: To-morrow! O, that's sudden! Spare him, spare him! He's not prepared for death. Even for our kitchens We kill the fowl of season: shall we serve heaven With less respect than we do minister To our gross selves? Good, good my lord, bethink you; Who is it that hath died for this offence? There's many have committed it.

trg: The law hath not been dead, though it hath slept: Those many had not dared to do that evil, If the first that did the edict infringe Had answer'd for his deed: now 'tis awake Takes note of what is done; and, like a prophet, Looks in a glass, that shows what future evils, Either new, or by remissness new-conceived, And so in progress to be hatch'd and born, Are now to have no successive degrees, But, ere they live, to end.

src: The law hath not been dead, though it hath slept: Those many had not dared to do that evil, If the first that did the edict infringe Had answer'd for his deed: now 'tis awake Takes note of what is done; and, like a prophet, Looks in a glass, that shows what future evils, Either new, or by remissness new-conceived, And so in progress to be hatch'd and born, Are now to have no successive degrees, But, ere they live, to end.
trg: Yet show some pity.

src: Yet show some pity.
trg: I show it most of all when I show justice; For then I pity those I do not know, Which a dismiss'd offence would after gall; And do him right that, answering one foul wrong, Lives not to act another. Be satisfied; Your brother dies to-morrow; be content.

trg: Could great men thunder As Jove himself does, Jove would ne'er be quiet, For every pelting, petty officer Would use his heaven for thunder; Nothing but thunder! trg: From thee, even from thy virtue! What's this, what's this? Is this her fault or mine? The tempter or the tempted, who sins most? Ha! Not she: nor doth she tempt: but it is I That, lying by the violet in the sun, Do as the carrion does, not as the flower, Corrupt with virtuous season. Can it be That modesty may more betray our sense Than woman's lightness? Having waste ground enough, Shall we desire to raze the sanctuary And pitch our evils there? O, fie, fie, fie! What dost thou, or what art thou, Angelo? Dost thou desire her foully for those things That make her good? O, let her brother live! Thieves for their robbery have authority When judges steal themselves. What, do I love her, That I desire to hear her speak again, And feast upon her eyes? What is't I dream on? O cunning enemy, that, to catch a saint, With saints dost bait thy hook! Most dangerous Is that temptation that doth goad us on To sin in loving virtue: never could the strumpet, With all her double vigour, art and nature, Once stir my temper; but this virtuous maid Subdues me quite. Even till now, When men were fond, I smiled and wonder'd how.

trg: When I would pray and think, I think and pray To several subjects. Heaven hath my empty words; Whilst my invention, hearing not my tongue, Anchors on Isabel: Heaven in my mouth, As if I did but only chew his name; And in my heart the strong and swelling evil Of my conception. The state, whereon I studied Is like a good thing, being often read, Grown fear'd and tedious; yea, my gravity, Wherein--let no man hear me--I take pride, Could I with boot change for an idle plume, Which the air beats for vain. O place, O form, How often dost thou with thy case, thy habit, Wrench awe from fools and tie the wiser souls To thy false seeming! Blood, thou art blood: Let's write good angel on the devil's horn: 'Tis not the devil's crest. How now! who's there?

trg: Who will believe thee, Isabel? My unsoil'd name, the austereness of my life, My vouch against you, and my place i' the state, Will so your accusation overweigh, That you shall stifle in your own report And smell of calumny. trg: To whom should I complain? Did I tell this, Who would believe me? O perilous mouths, That bear in them one and the self-same tongue, Either of condemnation or approof; Bidding the law make court'sy to their will: Hooking both right and wrong to the appetite, To follow as it draws! I'll to my brother: Though he hath fallen by prompture of the blood, Yet hath he in him such a mind of honour. That, had he twenty heads to tender down On twenty bloody blocks, he'ld yield them up, Before his sister should her body stoop To such abhorr'd pollution. Then, Isabel, live chaste, and, brother, die: More than our brother is our chastity. I'll tell him yet of Angelo's request, And fit his mind to death, for his soul's rest.

trg: Be absolute for death; either death or life Shall thereby be the sweeter. Reason thus with life: If I do lose thee, I do lose a thing That none but fools would keep: a breath thou art, Servile to all the skyey influences, That dost this habitation, where thou keep'st, Hourly afflict: merely, thou art death's fool; For him thou labour'st by thy flight to shun And yet runn'st toward him still. Thou art not noble; For all the accommodations that thou bear'st Are nursed by baseness. Thou'rt by no means valiant; For thou dost fear the soft and tender fork Of a poor worm. Thy best of rest is sleep, And that thou oft provokest; yet grossly fear'st Thy death, which is no more. Thou art not thyself; For thou exist'st on many a thousand grains That issue out of dust. Happy thou art not; For what thou hast not, still thou strivest to get, And what thou hast, forget'st. Thou art not certain; For thy complexion shifts to strange effects, After the moon. If thou art rich, thou'rt poor; For, like an ass whose back with ingots bows, Thou bear's thy heavy riches but a journey, And death unloads thee. Friend hast thou none; For thine own bowels, which do call thee sire, The mere effusion of thy proper loins, Do curse the gout, serpigo, and the rheum, For ending thee no sooner. Thou hast nor youth nor age, But, as it were, an after-dinner's sleep, Dreaming on both; for all thy blessed youth Becomes as aged, and doth beg the alms Of palsied eld; and when thou art old and rich, Thou hast neither heat, affection, limb, nor beauty, To make thy riches pleasant. What's yet in this That bears the name of life? Yet in this life Lie hid moe thousand deaths: yet death we fear, That makes these odds all even.

Friend hast thou none; For thine own bowels, which do call thee sire, The mere effusion of thy proper loins, Do curse the gout, serpigo, and the rheum, For ending thee no sooner. Thou hast nor youth nor age, But, as it were, an after-dinner's sleep, Dreaming on both; for all thy blessed youth Becomes as aged, and doth beg the alms Of palsied eld; and when thou art old and rich, Thou hast neither heat, affection, limb, nor beauty, To make thy riches pleasant. What's yet in this That bears the name of life? Yet in this life Lie hid moe thousand deaths: yet death we fear, That makes these odds all even.

src: It was a mad fantastical trick of him to steal from the state, and usurp the beggary he was never born to. Lord Angelo dukes it well in his absence; he puts transgression to 't.
trg: He does well in 't.

src: He does well in 't.
trg: A little more lenity to lechery would do no harm in him: something too crabbed that way, friar.

src: A little more lenity to lechery would do no harm in him: something too crabbed that way, friar.
trg: It is too general a vice, and severity must cure it.

src: It is too general a vice, and severity must cure it.
trg: Yes, in good sooth, the vice is of a great kindred; it is well allied: but it is impossible to extirp it quite, friar, till eating and drinking be put down. They say this Angelo was not made by man and woman after this downright way of creation: is it true, think you?

src: Yes, in good sooth, the vice is of a great kindred; it is well allied: but it is impossible to extirp it quite, friar, till eating and drinking be put down. They say this Angelo was not made by man and woman after this downright way of creation: is it true, think you?
trg: How should he be made, then?

src: How should he be made, then?
trg: Some report a sea-maid spawned him; some, that he was begot between two stock-fishes. But it is certain that when he makes water his urine is congealed ice; that I know to be true: and he is a motion generative; that's infallible.

src: Some report a sea-maid spawned him; some, that he was begot between two stock-fishes. But it is certain that when he makes water his urine is congealed ice; that I know to be true: and he is a motion generative; that's infallible.
trg: You are pleasant, sir, and speak apace.

src: You are pleasant, sir, and speak apace.
trg: Why, what a ruthless thing is this in him, for the rebellion of a codpiece to take away the life of a man! Would the duke that is absent have done this? Ere he would have hanged a man for the getting a hundred bastards, he would have paid for the nursing a thousand: he had some feeling of the sport: he knew the service, and that instructed him to mercy.

src: Why, what a ruthless thing is this in him, for the rebellion of a codpiece to take away the life of a man! Would the duke that is absent have done this? trg: I never heard the absent duke much detected for women; he was not inclined that way.

src: I never heard the absent duke much detected for women; he was not inclined that way.
trg: O, sir, you are deceived.

src: O, sir, you are deceived.
trg: 'Tis not possible.

src: 'Tis not possible.
trg: Who, not the duke? yes, your beggar of fifty; and his use was to put a ducat in her clack-dish: the duke had crotchets in him. He would be drunk too; that let me inform you.

src: Who, not the duke? yes, your beggar of fifty; and his use was to put a ducat in her clack-dish: the duke had crotchets in him. He would be drunk too; that let me inform you.
trg: You do him wrong, surely.

src: You do him wrong, surely.
trg: Sir, I was an inward of his. A shy fellow was the duke: and I believe I know the cause of his withdrawing.

src: Sir, I was an inward of his. A shy fellow was the duke: and I believe I know the cause of his withdrawing.
trg: What, I prithee, might be the cause?

src: What, I prithee, might be the cause?
trg: No, pardon; 'tis a secret must be locked within the teeth and the lips: but this I can let you understand, the greater file of the subject held the duke to be wise.

src: No, pardon; 'tis a secret must be locked within the teeth and the lips: but this I can let you understand, the greater file of the subject held the duke to be wise.
trg: Wise! why, no question but he was.

src: Wise! why, no question but he was.
trg: A very superficial, ignorant, unweighing fellow.

src: A very superficial, ignorant, unweighing fellow.
trg: Either this is the envy in you, folly, or mistaking: the very stream of his life and the business he hath helmed must upon a warranted need give him a better proclamation. Let him be but testimonied in his own bringings-forth, and he shall appear to the envious a scholar, a statesman and a soldier. Therefore you speak unskilfully: or if your knowledge be more it is much darkened in your malice.

trg: Sir, I know him, and I love him.

src: Sir, I know him, and I love him.
trg: Love talks with better knowledge, and knowledge with dearer love.

src: Love talks with better knowledge, and knowledge with dearer love.
trg: Come, sir, I know what I know.

src: Come, sir, I know what I know.
trg: I can hardly believe that, since you know not what you speak. But, if ever the duke return, as our prayers are he may, let me desire you to make your answer before him. If it be honest you have spoke, you have courage to maintain it: I am bound to call upon you; and, I pray you, your name?

src: I can hardly believe that, since you know not what you speak. But, if ever the duke return, as our prayers are he may, let me desire you to make your answer before him. If it be honest you have spoke, you have courage to maintain it: I am bound to call upon you; and, I pray you, your name?
trg: Sir, my name is Lucio; well known to the duke.

src: Sir, my name is Lucio; well known to the duke.
trg: He shall know you better, sir, if I may live to report you.

src: He shall know you better, sir, if I may live to report you.
trg: I fear you not.

src: I fear you not.
trg: O, you hope the duke will return no more; or you imagine me too unhurtful an opposite. But indeed I can do you little harm; you'll forswear this again.

src: O, you hope the duke will return no more; or you imagine me too unhurtful an opposite. But indeed I can do you little harm; you'll forswear this again.
trg: I'll be hanged first: thou art deceived in me, friar. But no more of this. Canst thou tell if Claudio die to-morrow or no?

src: I'll be hanged first: thou art deceived in me, friar. But no more of this. Canst thou tell if Claudio die to-morrow or no?
trg: Why should he die, sir?

src: Why should he die, sir?
trg: Why? For filling a bottle with a tundish. I would the duke we talk of were returned again: the ungenitured agent will unpeople the province with continency; sparrows must not build in his house-eaves, because they are lecherous. The duke yet would have dark deeds darkly answered; he would never bring them to light: would he were returned! Marry, this Claudio is condemned for untrussing. Farewell, good friar: I prithee, pray for me. The duke, I say to thee again, would eat mutton on Fridays. He's not past it yet, and I say to thee, he would mouth with a beggar, though she smelt brown bread and garlic: say that I said so. Farewell.

trg: Go; away with her to prison!

src: Go; away with her to prison!
trg: Good my lord, be good to me; your honour is accounted a merciful man; good my lord.

src: Good my lord, be good to me; your honour is accounted a merciful man; good my lord.
trg: Double and treble admonition, and still forfeit in the same kind! This would make mercy swear and play the tyrant.

src: Double and treble admonition, and still forfeit in the same kind! This would make mercy swear and play the tyrant.
trg: A bawd of eleven years' continuance, may it please your honour.

src: A bawd of eleven years' continuance, may it please your honour.
trg: My lord, this is one Lucio's information against me. Mistress Kate Keepdown was with child by him in the duke's time; he promised her marriage: his child is a year and a quarter old, come Philip and Jacob: I have kept it myself; and see how he goes about to abuse me!

trg: That fellow is a fellow of much licence: let him be called before us. Away with her to prison! Go to; no more words. Provost, my brother Angelo will not be altered; Claudio must die to-morrow: let him be furnished with divines, and have all charitable preparation. if my brother wrought by my pity, it should not be so with him.

trg: So please you, this friar hath been with him, and advised him for the entertainment of death.

src: So please you, this friar hath been with him, and advised him for the entertainment of death.
trg: Good even, good father.

src: Good even, good father.
trg: Bliss and goodness on you!

src: Bliss and goodness on you!
trg: Of whence are you?

src: Of whence are you?
trg: Not of this country, though my chance is now To use it for my time: I am a brother Of gracious order, late come from the See In special business from his holiness.

src: Not of this country, though my chance is now To use it for my time: I am a brother Of gracious order, late come from the See In special business from his holiness.
trg: What news abroad i' the world?

src: What news abroad i' the world?
trg: None, but that there is so great a fever on goodness, that the dissolution of it must cure it: novelty is only in request; and it is as dangerous to be aged in any kind of course, as it is virtuous to be constant in any undertaking. There is scarce truth enough alive to make societies secure; but security enough to make fellowships accurst: much upon this riddle runs the wisdom of the world. This news is old enough, yet it is every day's news. I pray you, sir, of what disposition was the duke?

src: One that, above all other strifes, contended especially to know himself.
trg: What pleasure was he given to?

src: What pleasure was he given to?
trg: Rather rejoicing to see another merry, than merry at any thing which professed to make him rejoice: a gentleman of all temperance. But leave we him to his events, with a prayer they may prove prosperous; and let me desire to know how you find Claudio prepared. I am made to understand that you have lent him visitation.

trg: He professes to have received no sinister measure from his judge, but most willingly humbles himself to the determination of justice: yet had he framed to himself, by the instruction of his frailty, many deceiving promises of life; which I by my good leisure have discredited to him, and now is he resolved to die.

src: He professes to have received no sinister measure from his judge, but most willingly humbles himself to the determination of justice: yet had he framed to himself, by the instruction of his frailty, many deceiving promises of life; which I by my good leisure have discredited to him, and now is he resolved to die.
trg: You have paid the heavens your function, and the prisoner the very debt of your calling. I have laboured for the poor gentleman to the extremest shore of my modesty: but my brother justice have I found so severe, that he hath forced me to tell him he is indeed Justice.

src: You have paid the heavens your function, and the prisoner the very debt of your calling. I have laboured for the poor gentleman to the extremest shore of my modesty: but my brother justice have I found so severe, that he hath forced me to tell him he is indeed Justice.
trg: If his own life answer the straitness of his proceeding, it shall become him well; wherein if he chance to fail, he hath sentenced himself.

src: If his own life answer the straitness of his proceeding, it shall become him well; wherein if he chance to fail, he hath sentenced himself.
trg: I am going to visit the prisoner. Fare you well.

src: I am going to visit the prisoner. Fare you well.
trg: Peace be with you! He who the sword of heaven will bear Should be as holy as severe; Pattern in himself to know, Grace to stand, and virtue go; More nor less to others paying Than by self-offences weighing. Shame to him whose cruel striking Kills for faults of his own liking! Twice treble shame on Angelo, To weed my vice and let his grow! O, what may man within him hide, Though angel on the outward side! How may likeness made in crimes, Making practise on the times, To draw with idle spiders' strings Most ponderous and substantial things! Craft against vice I must apply: With Angelo to-night shall lie His old betrothed but despised; So disguise shall, by the disguised, Pay with falsehood false exacting, And perform an old contracting.

trg: MARIANA: Break off thy song, and haste thee quick away: Here comes a man of comfort, whose advice Hath often still'd my brawling discontent. I cry you mercy, sir; and well could wish You had not found me here so musical: Let me excuse me, and believe me so, My mirth it much displeased, but pleased my woe.

src: MARIANA: Break off thy song, and haste thee quick away: Here comes a man of comfort, whose advice Hath often still'd my brawling discontent. I cry you mercy, sir; and well could wish You had not found me here so musical: Let me excuse me, and believe me so, My mirth it much displeased, but pleased my woe.
trg: 'Tis good; though music oft hath such a charm To make bad good, and good provoke to harm. I pray, you, tell me, hath any body inquired for me here to-day? much upon this time have I promised here to meet.

src: 'Tis good; though music oft hath such a charm To make bad good, and good provoke to harm. I pray, you, tell me, hath any body inquired for me here to-day? much upon this time have I promised here to meet.
trg: You have not been inquired after: I have sat here all day.

src: You have not been inquired after: I have sat here all day.
trg: I do constantly believe you. The time is come even now. I shall crave your forbearance a little: may be I will call upon you anon, for some advantage to yourself.

src: I do constantly believe you. The time is come even now. I shall crave your forbearance a little: may be I will call upon you anon, for some advantage to yourself.
trg: I am always bound to you.

src: I am always bound to you.
trg: Very well met, and well come. What is the news from this good deputy?

src: Very well met, and well come. What is the news from this good deputy?
trg: He hath a garden circummured with brick, Whose western side is with a vineyard back'd; And to that vineyard is a planched gate, That makes his opening with this bigger key: This other doth command a little door Which from the vineyard to the garden leads; There have I made my promise Upon the heavy middle of the night To call upon him.

trg: But shall you on your knowledge find this way?

src: But shall you on your knowledge find this way?
trg: I have ta'en a due and wary note upon't: With whispering and most guilty diligence, In action all of precept, he did show me The way twice o'er.

src: I have ta'en a due and wary note upon't: With whispering and most guilty diligence, In action all of precept, he did show me The way twice o'er.

src: Are there no other tokens Between you 'greed concerning her observance?
trg: No, none, but only a repair i' the dark; And that I have possess'd him my most stay Can be but brief; for I have made him know I have a servant comes with me along, That stays upon me, whose persuasion is I come about my brother.

src: Do you persuade yourself that I respect you?

src: Good friar, I know you do, and have found it.
trg: Take, then, this your companion by the hand, Who hath a story ready for your ear. I shall attend your leisure: but make haste; The vaporous night approaches.

trg: Will't please you walk aside?

src: Will't please you walk aside?
trg: O place and greatness! millions of false eyes Are stuck upon thee: volumes of report Run with these false and most contrarious quests Upon thy doings: thousand escapes of wit Make thee the father of their idle dreams And rack thee in their fancies. Welcome, how agreed?

src: She'll take the enterprise upon her, father, If you advise it.
trg: It is not my consent, But my entreaty too.

src: It is not my consent, But my entreaty too.
trg: Little have you to say When you depart from him, but, soft and low, 'Remember now my brother.'

src: Little have you to say When you depart from him, but, soft and low, 'Remember now my brother.'
trg: Fear me not.

src: Fear me not.
trg: Nor, gentle daughter, fear you not at all. He is your husband on a pre-contract: To bring you thus together, 'tis no sin, Sith that the justice of your title to him Doth flourish the deceit. Come, let us go: Our corn's to reap, for yet our tithe's to sow.

src: Come hither, sirrah. Can you cut off a man's head?
trg: If the man be a bachelor, sir, I can; but if he be a married man, he's his wife's head, and I can never cut off a woman's head.

trg: Come, sir, leave me your snatches, and yield me a direct answer. To-morrow morning are to die Claudio and Barnardine. src: Not so, not so; his life is parallel'd Even with the stroke and line of his great justice: He doth with holy abstinence subdue That in himself which he spurs on his power To qualify in others: were he meal'd with that Which he corrects, then were he tyrannous; But this being so, he's just. Now are they come. This is a gentle provost: seldom when The steeled gaoler is the friend of men. How now! what noise? That spirit's possessed with haste That wounds the unsisting postern with these strokes.
trg: There he must stay until the officer Arise to let him in: he is call'd up.

src: There he must stay until the officer Arise to let him in: he is call'd up.
trg: Have you no countermand for Claudio yet, But he must die to-morrow?

src: Have you no countermand for Claudio yet, But he must die to-morrow?
trg: None, sir, none.

src: None, sir, none.
trg: As near the dawning, provost, as it is, You shall hear more ere morning.

src: As near the dawning, provost, as it is, You shall hear more ere morning.
trg: Happily You something know; yet I believe there comes No countermand; no such example have we: Besides, upon the very siege of justice Lord Angelo hath to the public ear Profess'd the contrary. This is his lordship's man.

src: Happily You something know; yet I believe there comes No countermand; no such example have we: Besides, upon the very siege of justice Lord Angelo hath to the public ear Profess'd the contrary. This is his lordship's man.
trg: And here comes Claudio's pardon.

src: And here comes Claudio's pardon.

trg: I shall obey him.

src: I shall obey him.

trg: I told you. Lord Angelo, belike thinking me remiss in mine office, awakens me with this unwonted putting-on; methinks strangely, for he hath not used it before.

src: I told you. Lord Angelo, belike thinking me remiss in mine office, awakens me with this unwonted putting-on; methinks strangely, for he hath not used it before.
trg: Pray you, let's hear.

src: Pray you, let's hear.

trg: What is that Barnardine who is to be executed in the afternoon?

src: What is that Barnardine who is to be executed in the afternoon?
trg: A Bohemian born, but here nursed un and bred; one that is a prisoner nine years old.

src: A Bohemian born, but here nursed un and bred; one that is a prisoner nine years old.
trg: How came it that the absent duke had not either delivered him to his liberty or executed him? I have heard it was ever his manner to do so.

src: How came it that the absent duke had not either delivered him to his liberty or executed him? I have heard it was ever his manner to do so.
trg: His friends still wrought reprieves for him: and, indeed, his fact, till now in the government of Lord Angelo, came not to an undoubtful proof.

src: His friends still wrought reprieves for him: and, indeed, his fact, till now in the government of Lord Angelo, came not to an undoubtful proof.
trg: It is now apparent?

src: It is now apparent?
trg: Most manifest, and not denied by himself.

src: Most manifest, and not denied by himself.
trg: Hath he born himself penitently in prison? how seems he to be touched?

src: Hath he born himself penitently in prison? how seems he to be touched?
trg: A man that apprehends death no more dreadfully but as a drunken sleep; careless, reckless, and fearless of what's past, present, or to come; insensible of mortality, and desperately mortal.

src: A man that apprehends death no more dreadfully but as a drunken sleep; careless, reckless, and fearless of what's past, present, or to come; insensible of mortality, and desperately mortal.
trg: He wants advice.

src: He wants advice.
trg: He will hear none: he hath evermore had the liberty of the prison; give him leave to escape hence, he would not: drunk many times a day, if not many days entirely drunk. We have very oft awaked him, as if to carry him to execution, and showed him a seeming warrant for it: it hath not moved him at all.

src: He will hear none: he hath evermore had the liberty of the prison; give him leave to escape hence, he would not: drunk many times a day, if not many days entirely drunk. We have very oft awaked him, as if to carry him to execution, and showed him a seeming warrant for it: it hath not moved him at all.
trg: More of him anon. There is written in your brow, provost, honesty and constancy: if I read it not truly, my ancient skill beguiles me; but, in the boldness of my cunning, I will lay myself in hazard. Claudio, whom here you have warrant to execute, is no greater forfeit to the law than Angelo who hath sentenced him. To make you understand this in a manifested effect, I crave but four days' respite; for the which you are to do me both a present and a dangerous courtesy.

trg: Pray, sir, in what?

src: Pray, sir, in what?
trg: In the delaying death.

src: In the delaying death.
trg: A lack, how may I do it, having the hour limited, and an express command, under penalty, to deliver his head in the view of Angelo? I may make my case as Claudio's, to cross this in the smallest.

src: A lack, how may I do it, having the hour limited, and an express command, under penalty, to deliver his head in the view of Angelo? I may make my case as Claudio's, to cross this in the smallest.
trg: By the vow of mine order I warrant you, if my instructions may be your guide. Let this Barnardine be this morning executed, and his head born to Angelo.

src: By the vow of mine order I warrant you, if my instructions may be your guide. Let this Barnardine be this morning executed, and his head born to Angelo.
trg: Angelo hath seen them both, and will discover the favour.

src: Angelo hath seen them both, and will discover the favour.
trg: O, death's a great disguiser; and you may add to it. Shave the head, and tie the beard; and say it was the desire of the penitent to be so bared before his death: you know the course is common. If any thing fall to you upon this, more than thanks and good fortune, by the saint whom I profess, I will plead against it with my life.

src: O, death's a great disguiser; and you may add to it. Shave the head, and tie the beard; and say it was the desire of the penitent to be so bared before his death: you know the course is common. trg: Pardon me, good father; it is against my oath.

src: Pardon me, good father; it is against my oath.
trg: Were you sworn to the duke, or to the deputy?

src: Were you sworn to the duke, or to the deputy?
trg: To him, and to his substitutes.

src: To him, and to his substitutes.
trg: You will think you have made no offence, if the duke avouch the justice of your dealing?

src: You will think you have made no offence, if the duke avouch the justice of your dealing?
trg: But what likelihood is in that?

src: But what likelihood is in that?
trg: Not a resemblance, but a certainty. Yet since I see you fearful, that neither my coat, integrity, nor persuasion can with ease attempt you, I will go further than I meant, to pluck all fears out of you. Look you, sir, here is the hand and seal of the duke: you know the character, I doubt not; and the signet is not strange to you.

src: Not a resemblance, but a certainty. Yet since I see you fearful, that neither my coat, integrity, nor persuasion can with ease attempt you, I will go further than I meant, to pluck all fears out of you. Look you, sir, here is the hand and seal of the duke: you know the character, I doubt not; and the signet is not strange to you.
trg: I know them both.

src: I know them both.
trg: The contents of this is the return of the duke: you shall anon over-read it at your pleasure; where you shall find, within these two days he will be here. This is a thing that Angelo knows not; for he this very day receives letters of strange tenor; perchance of the duke's death; perchance entering into some monastery; but, by chance, nothing of what is writ. Look, the unfolding star calls up the shepherd. Put not yourself into amazement how these things should be: all difficulties are but easy when they are known. Call your executioner, and off with Barnardine's head: I will give him a present shrift and advise him for a better place. Yet you are amazed; but this shall absolutely resolve you. Come away; it is almost clear dawn.

trg: I am as well acquainted here as I was in our house of profession: one would think it were Mistress Overdone's own house, for here be many of her old customers. First, here's young Master Rash; he's in for a commodity of brown paper and old ginger, ninescore and seventeen pounds; of which he made five marks, ready money: marry, then ginger was not much in request, for the old women were all dead. Then is there here one Master Caper, at the suit of Master Three-pile the mercer, for some four suits of peach-coloured satin, which now peaches him a beggar. Then have we here young Dizy, and young Master Deep-vow, and Master Copperspur, and Master Starve-lackey the rapier and dagger man, and young Drop-heir that killed lusty Pudding, and Master Forthlight the tilter, and brave Master Shooty the great traveller, and wild Half-can that stabbed Pots, and, I think, forty more; all great doers in our trade, and are now 'for the Lord's sake.'
